meta.title: Cities, counties and state preemption, 19 days of posts
meta.subject: the relationship between the Texas Legislature and cities and counties — state preemption of local ordinances, property tax revenue caps and the 3.5% limit, unfunded mandates on counties, jail and indigent defense costs, annexation and ETJ rules, and municipal and county associations' fights with the state
meta.subtitle: Oct 1 to Oct 19, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about Texas cities, counties and state preemption, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Local control as campaign attack
lanes.description: Candidates and activists attack Abbott, the Legislature or state agencies for taking decisions away from local school boards, cities and communities, and promise to restore local control.

lanes.label: State must rein in liberal cities
lanes.description: Preemption is defended as necessary to stop Austin, Houston, Dallas and San Antonio from passing woke, anti-business or anti-police ordinances that conflict with state law.

lanes.label: Revenue caps starve local services
lanes.description: The 3.5% property tax revenue cap and other state limits are blamed for squeezing police, fire, EMS and infrastructure budgets and forcing cities and counties into cuts or service reductions.

lanes.label: Local overspending demands tax relief
lanes.description: Cities and counties are portrayed as wasteful spenders whose property tax hikes justify state caps, appraisal limits and tougher limits on local debt and spending.

lanes.label: State pushes costs onto counties
lanes.description: The state is accused of dumping jail, indigent defense, bail, courts and border-related costs on counties without paying for them, while counties and their associations push back.

lanes.label: Annexation and ETJ fights
lanes.description: Debate over whether limits on annexation and extraterritorial jurisdiction protect landowners from city control or hamper orderly growth, services and development rules.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.
